juce::WaitableEvent Class Reference

## Detailed Description

Allows threads to wait for events triggered by other threads.

A thread can call [WaitableEvent::wait()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1WaitableEvent.html#ac38aeb80078cc4f3d3b5f32e230d6988 "Suspends the calling thread until the event has been signalled.") to suspend the calling thread until another thread wakes it up by calling the [WaitableEvent::signal()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1WaitableEvent.html#aa3a20faa489e012718f6e23690d85a8d "Wakes up any threads that are currently waiting on this object.") method.

Suspends the calling thread until the event has been signalled.

This will wait until the object's [signal()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1WaitableEvent.html#aa3a20faa489e012718f6e23690d85a8d "Wakes up any threads that are currently waiting on this object.") method is called by another thread, or until the timeout expires.

After the event has been signalled, this method will return true and if manualReset was set to false in the [WaitableEvent](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1WaitableEvent.html "Allows threads to wait for events triggered by other threads.")'s constructor, then the event will be reset.

If the [WaitableEvent](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1WaitableEvent.html "Allows threads to wait for events triggered by other threads.") is manual reset, all current and future threads that wait upon this object will be woken, until [reset()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1WaitableEvent.html#ab7b611ccd10e74a72c00bed71ea761ee "Resets the event to an unsignalled state.") is explicitly called.

juce::WaitableEvent Class Reference

Detailed Description

Allows threads to wait for events triggered by other threads.

A thread can call WaitableEvent::wait() to suspend the calling thread until another thread wakes it up by calling the WaitableEvent::signal() method.

◆ wait()

bool juce::WaitableEvent::wait ( double timeOutMilliseconds = -1.0) const

Suspends the calling thread until the event has been signalled.

This will wait until the object's signal() method is called by another thread, or until the timeout expires.

After the event has been signalled, this method will return true and if manualReset was set to false in the WaitableEvent's constructor, then the event will be reset.

Parameters
timeOutMillisecondsthe maximum time to wait, in milliseconds. A negative value will cause it to wait forever.
Returns
true if the object has been signalled, false if the timeout expires first.
See also
signal, reset

◆ signal()

void juce::WaitableEvent::signal ( ) const

Wakes up any threads that are currently waiting on this object.

If signal() is called when nothing is waiting, the next thread to call wait() will return immediately and reset the signal.

If the WaitableEvent is manual reset, all current and future threads that wait upon this object will be woken, until reset() is explicitly called.

If the WaitableEvent is automatic reset, and one or more threads is waiting upon the object, then one of them will be woken up. If no threads are currently waiting, then the next thread to call wait() will be woken up. As soon as a thread is woken, the signal is automatically reset.

wait, reset
